first_step_test: One long narrow thorax joined to one tapered abdomen fixes the mantis body angle and leaves clear attachment space for the head and six legs.

source.notes: Planned as one six-panel cumulative graphite and restrained colored-pencil contact sheet; rejected iterations, if any, remain private under the slug draft folder.

final_elements.description: One long narrow thorax joined to one gently curved tapered abdomen, angled from lower left to upper right.

final_elements.description: One small triangular head attached to the thorax with exactly two long curved antennae.

final_elements.description: One almond-shaped near eye with one small paper highlight.

final_elements.description: One clearly visible bent grasping foreleg attached near the front of the thorax with a row of short inner spines; the far foreleg stays hidden in side view.

final_elements.description: Exactly four long walking legs attached beneath the middle and rear body, with their feet meeting one diagonal twig.

frames.visible_job: Draws the connected narrow thorax and tapered abdomen on one rising diagonal.
frames.instruction: Draw one long narrow thorax rising from lower left to upper right, then join its rear end to one gently curved abdomen that tapers to a soft point. Leave the front end open enough for the head and keep clear paper beneath both forms for the legs.

frames.visible_job: Adds the attached triangular head, two curved antennae, and one visible eye.
frames.instruction: Attach a small rounded triangle to the front of the thorax and tilt its point slightly downward. Sweep exactly two thin antennae from the top corners, then place one almond-shaped near eye with a tiny open-paper highlight.

frames.visible_job: Adds one angular folded foreleg with a row of short inner spines.
frames.instruction: From the front of the thorax, angle one visible upper foreleg section down and forward, fold its lower section back toward the head, and add a short row of inner spines. Let the far foreleg remain hidden in this clean side view.

frames.step_name: Plant four legs on the twig
frames.visible_job: Adds exactly four long walking legs and one diagonal twig behind their feet.
frames.instruction: Attach exactly four long walking legs beneath the middle and rear body, bending each once at a clear knee. Draw one diagonal twig behind the feet so every foot meets its upper edge, stopping the twig line wherever a leg overlaps it.

frames.visible_job: Adds one folded wing, three abdomen bands, two twig leaves, and one broken shadow.
frames.instruction: Lay one long leaf-shaped folded wing over the near abdomen, add exactly three short curved bands on the exposed rear section, attach exactly two simple leaves to open parts of the twig, and place one light broken graphite shadow beneath the mantis.

final_step.visible_job: Layers olive, leaf green, warm brown, and graphite only over established forms.
final_step.instruction: Layer pale olive over the established body and five visible legs, deepen the folded wing and two leaves with muted green, warm the twig with brown, and reinforce the same broken shadow with graphite. Keep the two antennae, eye highlight, foreleg spines, and three abdomen bands visible without adding contours.

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first saved crop contains only one connected long thorax and tapered abdomen on their final rising diagonal. The head end and the paper beneath the body remain open for later attachments, so a learner can place the main proportion without guessing at legs or scenery.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: I compared all six saved crops pairwise at full size. The body, head, antennae, eye, folded foreleg, four walking legs, twig, wing, three abdomen bands, two leaves, and shadow keep their anchors; each step has one readable addition, and the finish adds only restrained color and graphite depth.
